title: Neuro-Symbolic Meta-Policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory under Partial Observability
abstract: arXiv:2607.18368v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Partially observable reinforcement learning requires deciding what to retain, retrieve, and forget over time. We introduce a neuro-symbolic meta-policy that learns which symbolic memory heuristic to apply at each decision point while keeping execution symbolic. Our setting uses temporal knowledge-graph memory in RoomKG, where hidden state and observations are represented as Resource Description Framework (RDF) graphs and memory is augmented with temporal RDF triple annotations. The model combines knowledge-graph encoding of memory contents with value heads for question answering, exploration, and forgetting, yielding a controller that is both adaptive and inspectable. This gives the work a direct Semantic Web grounding through RDF-based representation, annotation-compatible graph semantics, and graph-based symbolic operations over explicit memory state. tldr: 本文提出一种神经符号元策略，在部分可观测强化学习中学习在每个决策点选择合适的符号记忆启发式方法，并结合基于RDF的时序知识图谱记忆，实现了自适应且可检查的记忆保留、检索与遗忘控制。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a neuro-symbolic meta-policy that learns which symbolic memory heuristic to apply at each decision point in partially observable reinforcement learning, leveraging temporal RDF knowledge-graph memory to achieve adaptive and inspectable retention, retrieval, and forgetting of memory contents.
